l: A. Employees are evaluated on six (6) values, plus a number of goals set by their supervisor. The Performance Standards define the values and describe performance standards for each value. TBP 4.08

B. Every employee is required to be evaluated annually. The performance evaluation review period for all employees is October 1 to September 30. Although a formal evaluation process is not required mid-year, an informal check-in evaluation will occur in April of each year. TBP 4.08 and TBP 4.09

New non-sworn employees will receive an informal review at the conclusion of their probation six (6) months after their hire date. The employee’s formal review will occur in October with the rest of the department.
1. The Meet and Confer Contract shall be referenced for specific information related to the probationary period for newly hired officers, lateral officers, and reappointed officers.

Employees who have been promoted or transferred will receive their reviews during the annual performance review. If the employee has been under the supervision of their current supervisor for two (2) months or less, the preceding supervisor will complete the evaluation and provide it to the current supervisor of the employee. If the employee has worked for the current supervisor for more than two (2) months, but less than the entire performance period, then the current supervisor will confer with the previous supervisor and consider their input when preparing the performance appraisal. TBP 4.09
E. Employees on Medical Leave or Military Leave

If the employee worked less than two (2) months of the performance period, the employee will not be evaluated for that performance period. If the employee worked two (2) months or more of the performance period, the supervisor will complete the performance appraisal as scheduled, pro-rating performance measures as appropriate.

1. If the employee is on leave at the time the performance appraisal is due, the supervisor can complete the evaluation as scheduled and submit the performance appraisal via ePerformance. The supervisor may contact City HRIS to have the ePerformance document reopened in order to add comments, finalize, etc. when the employee returns from leave.
2. If the performance review has not been submitted in ePerformance due to the employee’s absence, upon the employee’s return, the supervisor can submit the evaluation. TBP 4.08 and TBP 4.09

3. Any issues covered by or related to the Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) should not be addressed within the Performance Evaluation process. Feedback should be performance specific, not related to circumstances that are beyond the employee’s control.

1. All supervisors evaluating officers who have been approved to carry a Conducted Electrical Weapon (CEW) will conduct a review of the officer’s CEW data for the mid-year check-in and for the annual ePerformance process, and will reconcile the Taser Use of Force reports with the information from the review. The supervisor will also review the information for patterns of use. The supervisor will discuss the recorded use of the CEW with the officer to ensure the officer is in compliance with departmental policy. Any non-compliance by the officer with the department’s use of force policy shall be reflected on the officer’s mid-year check-in (April) and the annual ePerformance process (October). TBP 4.08 and TBP 4.09

2. At the time of the mid-year check-in (April) and the annual ePerformance process (October), each supervisor will conduct a body worn camera audit as required in General Order 506.03 (D)(7) for each officer assigned to them and document these audits in Blue Team.

3. The immediate supervisor shall then conduct a private interview with the officer being evaluated. Prior supervisors may take part in the interview. This interview shall be constructive in nature and the desired results shall be: TBP 4.08 and TBP 4.09
a. An understanding by the officer of the rating achieved during the period and the factors contributing to that rating.
b. Arrival at recommended constructive actions for the next evaluation period to improve upon any weak areas of performance.
c. Signatures are via employee comments and acknowledgements in ePerformance. This signature does not signify approval of the rating, but only signifies that the interview was held.

d. The captains and commanders shall meet with their respective deputy chief, the deputy chiefs shall meet with their respective assistant chiefs, and the assistant chiefs with the Chief of Police to discuss evaluation of their next in command before conducting a private interview with the lieutenant, captain, or deputy chief being evaluated.

e. All officers should be evaluated honestly and objectively. In evaluating these areas, the supervisor should also take into consideration such things as commendations, structured counseling sessions, attendance, personnel files, and verification with Internal Affairs for any complaints that are available for substantiating an individual’s rating.

f. Performance Appraisals and reviews shall not be subject to the grievance procedure, but may be appealed only to the next highest level in the chain of command above the grader. If the employee is in disagreement with the performance appraisal, the employee may attach an inter-office correspondence to the appraisal that must remain with that appraisal document.
g. A level-up supervisor cannot direct a reviewer to change their review of a subordinate. The level-up supervisor may provide comments in the designated area within the appraisal form.
h. Performance Appraisal forms are located in PeopleSoft, within the ePerformance tile. TBP 4.08
